province.subdivision_list: complete (no entries; cantons are not written in addresses)

CH.notes: UPU: canton abbreviation is appended to the locality only when the locality name is not unique (e.g. '1556 CERNIAZ VD'); users type it in the city field, so no %S needed. Swiss Post's UPU examples omit the 'CH-' prefix (country name on the last line instead); live keeps postprefix CH-, which is harmless. Live posturl (post.ch/db/owa/...) is dead.

dropped_tokens.%X: Two-digit delivery-office code written before 'B.P.' and after the locality ('06 B.P. 37 ABIDJAN 06'); UPU says it must be included. Not undeliverable if users type it in the street/city fields, but the form gives no prompt for it.

province.subdivision_list: complete (no entries; not used in addresses)

CI.notes: No postcodes. Delivery is mainly to P.O. boxes. UPU sheet is from 09/2004. If %X is not kept, recommend the layout '%N%n%O%n%A%n%C' and tell users to write the office code in the box line ('06 B.P. 37') and the city ('ABIDJAN 06').

CK.notes: No postcodes. The older repo had zip \d{4}; live removed it, which is correct. The city line holds the island name (RAROTONGA, AITUTAKI, ...).

province.subdivision_list: complete (16 regions including CL-NB Ñuble, created 2018)

changes_from_live: state_name_type: live dropped it, so the default is 'province'; Chile's first-level unit is the 'región' (provinces are a second level). Recommend 'region' (Google's enum has no 'region', so Google's default would mislabel it).
required: live default is AC; Correos de Chile's minimum-information example has the region on its own line, so recommend ACS.
CL.notes: Every commune has a commune-wide fallback code (xxx0000), so Z can always be filled; still not made required because few residents know block-face codes. The live posturl was dropped; www.correos.cl is the operator.

CM.notes: No postcodes; delivery is by BP (P.O. box) + town. The UPU sheet dates from 07/2002 and nothing newer was found.

dropped_tokens.%D: District/county (区/县). UPU Latin examples have it on its own line ('Haidian District'). Postcode plus street usually routes correctly, but in large cities the district is expected; if %D is not kept, users should put it on a street line.

province.subdivision_list: complete (34: 23 provinces, 5 autonomous regions, 4 municipalities, plus HK/MO/TW as in ISO 3166-2:CN and Google)

CN.notes: Latin-script order (lfmt) is '%N%n%O%n%A%n%D%n%C%n%S, %Z'; UPU writes the postcode before the province ('100004 BEIJING'). Sub-region overrides (sub_xzips/sub_xrequires) for HK/MO/TW should be kept if we import sub-rules.

dropped_tokens.%D: Sub-locality (barrio / 'Localidad de Kennedy'); UPU shows it on its own line. Put it in a street line if %D is dropped; low risk.

changes_from_live: required: live 'AS' does not require the city. Every 4-72 example has a locality, so recommend ACS. Decide whether Bogotá (state = city) should be exempt.
CO.notes: UPU 10/2022 writes 'BOGOTA 111711' (locality + postcode, then department on the next line), while live has '%C, %S, %Z' on one line. Both are accepted in practice. The live posturl codigopostal.gov.co is the 4-72 lookup.

dropped_tokens.%D: District (distrito): UPU writes 'Province, Canton, District' on one line. The 5-digit postcode identifies the district uniquely, so leaving %D out is low risk when Z is given.

province.subdivision_list: issues: no CR entries in subdivisions.tsv, yet live has %S required. Missing all 7 provinces: CR-A Alajuela, CR-C Cartago, CR-G Guanacaste, CR-H Heredia, CR-L Limón, CR-P Puntarenas, CR-SJ San José.

changes_from_live: zip: live '\d{4,5}|\d{3}-\d{4}' accepts obsolete 4-digit and apartado-style codes. Current codes are 5 digits (province digit, 2-digit canton, 2-digit district). For P.O. boxes, UPU writes 'box-postcode' ('3017-40601'); the box number belongs in the address line.
zipex: '1000,2010,1001' are obsolete 4-digit examples; replace with 5-digit ones.
CR.notes: Postcode recommended but not required (live does not require it; addresses commonly use landmarks).

dropped_tokens.%D: UPU shows a postal-zone line ('Habana 6') between street and postcode; it can go in a street line.

province.subdivision_list: complete (15 provinces + CU-99 Isla de la Juventud, post-2011 split of La Habana into Artemisa/Mayabeque)

changes_from_live: layout: live '%C %S%n%Z' puts the postcode alone on the last line. UPU (09/2004, the only official source found) writes 'CP 10600 CIUDAD HABANA' (prefix CP, code before locality). Recommend '%N%n%O%n%A%nCP %Z %C%n%S' and allowing an optional 'CP' prefix when parsing input.
CU.notes: Live is new (the repo had no data). Our only official source is from 2004, before the 2011 province reform, so neither layout can be confirmed as current practice.

province.subdivision_list: issues: islands are not ISO 3166-2:CV subdivisions (ISO lists 22 municipalities and 2 regions). CV-BV, CV-BR, CV-MA, CV-SL and CV-SV are municipality codes that happen to match single-municipality islands. CV-FOGO, CV-SANTIAGO, CV-SANTO_ANTAO and CV-SAO_NICOLAU are invented, non-ISO codes. Decide whether to keep island keys with private codes or drop the ISO pretence.

CV.notes: Address rules match live; the only issue is how the subdivision list is coded. Live sub_isoids is also blank for Fogo/Santiago/Santo Antão/São Nicolau.

province.subdivision_list: complete (no entries; %S is free text, always 'WA')

CX.notes: UPU defers to Australia. Australia Post lists 'CHRISTMAS ISLAND WA 6798'. Consider pre-filling S='WA' and Z='6798'. Australian rules would make CSZ required; live leaves them optional, which is harmless with a single code.

province.subdivision_list: complete (no entries; districts not written in addresses)

changes_from_live: required: live default AC; Cyprus Post (UPU 3/2023) puts a postcode in every address, so recommend ACZ.
Cyprus Post asks for the 'CY-' prefix on inbound international mail ('CY-2008 Strovolos'); consider postprefix 'CY-' and accepting an optional CY- prefix in input.
CY.notes: The northern part uses Turkish 'Mersin 10' routing with 99xxx codes, which this pattern does not cover (outside Cyprus Post's system).

CZ.notes: The line after the postcode may be the delivery post office ('102 00 Praha 102', 'PRAHA 3') rather than the locality; the locality then goes on the line above. Live posturl psc.ceskaposta.cz is stale.

DE.notes: Deutsche Post: never prefix 'D-'/'DE-'. Packstation addresses use the street lines (customer number + 'Packstation NNN').

changes_from_live: Live has no data (no zip, default layout). La Poste de Djibouti (UPU 05/2020) uses 5-digit codes '77' + region digit 1–6 + office (77101 DJIBOUTI VILLE … 77601 TADJOURAH), written to the left of the locality. Add zip/zipex and the layout '%Z %C'.
DJ.notes: Most delivery is to BP (P.O. box); the UPU format also allows a what3words line. Postcode not required because it maps 1:1 to the locality.

DK.notes: Live moved %N before %O (repo had %O first); this matches PostNord's line order (name, then att./company lines). The town after the code is the post-office town, and Copenhagen codes carry a suffix in the name ('1566 KØBENHAVN V'). Live posturl (postdanmark.dk) is dead; PostNord took over.

province.subdivision_list: complete (no entries; provinces not written in the UPU examples)

DO.notes: The UPU sheet (03/2005) has a sector line ('Katanga, Los Minas') above the postcode line; it fits in a street line. Postcodes are rarely used in practice.

province.subdivision_list: complete (no entries; wilaya not written separately)

DZ.notes: The first two digits are the wilaya number. Algeria went from 58 to 69 wilayas (announced 2025-11-16; law reported as April 2026), and some offices may be renumbered. \d{5} still covers this, but it could not be checked against an official Algérie Poste list. The UPU sheet is from 2002.

dropped_tokens.%D: UPU shows a sub-locality line ('Conocoto', 'Sector la Loma') above the postcode line; it fits in a street line.

changes_from_live: layout: live '%Z%n%C' puts the postcode and the locality on separate lines; UPU (09/2018) writes 'postcode - LOCALITY' on one line ('090306 - GUAYAQUIL').
The older repo pattern with letters/EC prefix is obsolete; live \d{6} is correct.
EC.notes: Correos del Ecuador was dissolved in 2020 and replaced by Servicios Postales del Ecuador, so live posturl codigopostal.gob.ec may be dead. Postcodes are rarely used, so they are not required.

province.subdivision_list: issues: no EE entries in subdivisions.tsv although live now has %S. changes_from_live: Subdivision list must be added (see province). The rules match live: in rural addresses the county ('VILJANDIMAA') takes the place of the town after the postcode, which live's '%Z %C %S' allows.
EE.notes: Verdict is 'corrected' only because of our subdivision list; live address data is fine.

changes_from_live: Pattern: Egypt Post's UPU sheet (07/2023) shows only 7-digit codes; the 7-digit system was completed in 2020. Live still accepts legacy 5-digit codes. Decide: strict '\d{7}' (official) or keep '\d{7}|\d{5}' while old codes stay in circulation (recommended for input).
state_name_type: 'governorate' (محافظة) instead of the default 'province'; not in Google's enum.
required: every UPU example includes the province (governorate) line; consider ACS.
EG.notes: Layout matches UPU: locality, then province, then postcode, each on its own line.

EH.notes: No UPU sheet (upu.int returns 302 for 'esh'). Mail is handled by Barid Al-Maghrib with Moroccan 5-digit codes (e.g. 70000 Laâyoune); examples not checked against an official list. Territory status is disputed; keep it neutral.

changes_from_live: layout: Correos (UPU 01/2013) writes the province on its own line below 'postcode LOCALITY'; live has '%Z %C %S' on one line.
pattern: the first two digits are the province number 01–52, so '\d{5}' accepts impossible codes such as 00xxx or 53xxx–99xxx. The tighter pattern is optional.
ES.notes: Both layouts are delivered; the change is cosmetic but follows the official guidance.

ET.notes: 4-digit codes exist (1000 = Addis Ababa) but are rarely used; most delivery is to P.O. boxes. The UPU sheet is from 2002.

province.subdivision_list: complete (no entries; Åland is a separate country code AX)

FI.notes: The UPU sheet (11/2024) omits the 'FI-' prefix; it is acceptable for international mail but not required. Codes ending in 1 are P.O. box codes.

FJ.notes: No postcodes. UPU sheet from 2004; an optional suburb line ('VATUWAQA') fits in the street lines.

FK.notes: Single postcode. Live removed the old %X line. Recommend accepting the code with or without the space.

province.subdivision_list: issues: no FM entries in subdivisions.tsv although live requires S. Missing all 4 states: FM-TRK Chuuk, FM-KSA Kosrae, FM-PNI Pohnpei, FM-YAP Yap.

changes_from_live: Subdivision list must be added (see province); live address rules are fine.
FM.notes: Follows USPS rules. ZIP per state: 96941 Pohnpei, 96942 Chuuk, 96943 Yap, 96944 Kosrae; a state–ZIP check is possible. USPS state abbreviation in addresses is 'FM'.

changes_from_live: postprefix: Posta's example (UPU 12/2017) is 'FO-100 Tórshavn', with a hyphen; live uses postprefix 'FO' with no hyphen and layout 'FO%Z', which renders 'FO100'. Recommend 'FO-'.
pattern: accept an optional typed 'FO'/'FO-' prefix.

dropped_tokens.%X: CEDEX (business mail). La Poste says 'never delete CEDEX'. Live already removed %X from fmt, so users type 'LIBOURNE CEDEX' or 'MONTPELLIER CEDEX 5' in the city field. Not undeliverable, but the city field must allow it.

FR.notes: The postcode for a CEDEX address can be a CEDEX-only code (e.g. 34092), so do not check it against geographic codes. Lieu-dit and building lines go in the street lines (up to 4 lines before the postcode).

GA.notes: The UPU sheet (07/2002) shows a 2-digit code before the locality and a delivery-office number after it ('01 LIBREVILLE–GROS-BOUQUET 03'), much like Côte d'Ivoire. These are not postcodes in general use; users can type them on the city line. Nothing newer found.

province.subdivision_list: complete (no entries; county no longer required by Royal Mail)

GB.notes: Live removed %S (county); this matches Royal Mail ('county no longer required if post town and postcode are given'). Dependent locality goes in the street lines. The pattern also accepts GY/JE/IM codes, which belong to other ISO countries; this is harmless. Live zipex 'BS18 8HF' is from the UPU sheet but BS18 was recoded (to BS40/48/49) years ago, so do not use it as an example.

GD.notes: No postcodes (UPU 10/2026). The city line is the parish/municipality (ST. GEORGE'S, ST. ANDREW'S).

dropped_tokens.%X: CEDEX, as for France; users type it in the city field.

changes_from_live: zip: live '9[78]3\d{2}' also accepts 983xx, which is not a French Guiana code (98x are Monaco/overseas collectivities). UPU: overseas codes start 97/98 and the third digit identifies the department, '3' = French Guiana, so all GF codes are 973xx.
GF.notes: Live fmt still contains %X (FR's live layout dropped it).

changes_from_live: layout: live hard-codes 'GUERNSEY' as the post-town line. That is right for Guernsey (GY1–GY8), but Alderney (GY9) and Sark (GY10) addresses use their own island names. Recommend '%N%n%O%n%A%n%C%n%Z' with %C = post town (GUERNSEY/ALDERNEY/SARK) and the parish in a street line. Not confirmed from a Guernsey Post source; the UPU sheet (2005) shows only a Guernsey example.
GG.notes: The UPU example also adds 'CHANNEL ISLANDS' after the postcode; it is optional.

dropped_tokens.%D: UPU line 4 (district / district capital), used only in some addresses; it can go in a street line.

changes_from_live: Live has no data. Ghana Post (UPU 03/2023) uses a postcode of 2 letters + '-' + 3 or 4 digits (GA-183), optionally extended by 4 digits into the GhanaPostGPS 'digital address' (GA-183-8164), written after the locality. The region is written on its own line.
GH.notes: Decisions needed: (1) accept the full digital address in the postal field or only the base code; (2) add the region list; (3) whether to require Z. Recommend: accept both forms, require AC only, region optional.

GI.notes: Single generic postcode. UPU: the locality line 'Gibraltar' sits above the postcode; live renders it as the literal. Recommend accepting the code with or without the space.
